newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil- Firm, interests on Taiwan tender.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil- Firm, interests on Taiwan tender.

text.p: Talks were thin in the Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market on Friday but sentiment was supported after Taiwan tendered to buy two 38,000-tonne cargoes for June delivery, traders said.
The 180-cst grade was heard offered at $99.50 per tonne, compared with Monday's $98.5 trading level, traders said.
The 380-cst grade was bid at $91.00 per tonne but no suppliers emerged, they said.
"Demand is just normal but sentiment was quite well supported," said one trader, noting fewer cargoes from Kuwait due to its summer demand at home.
On SIMEX, one 5,000-tonne cash deal was heard done based on SIMEX related prices, the first physical deal on SIMEX after the relaunch of the fuel oil futures contract on April 22, traders said.
On demand, Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has issued a tender to buy two 0.5-percent 38,000-tonne cargoes of fuel oil for June delivery.
CPC seeks to buy one low-pour cargo for delivery June 11-30 and one high-pour cargo for delivery June 1-30, both to Keelung Taichung or Shenao on a cost-and-freight basis (c-and-f).
The tender closes on May 7 and is valid for two days.
"The CPC tender result should bring some fresh indications to the current slow market," said one trader.
The LSWR market remained listless, with ample supplies and poor demand, traders said.
